description: BUG 2: Mouse still behaves erratically despite the v0.5.1 atomic snapshot fix. The current model forwards ALL mouse messages to ImGui while the overlay is visible and consumes them when g_wantCaptureMouse is true, which lets the panel fight the game for the mouse. Replace this with a modifier-gated model: the overlay is 100% passive by default (never intercepts mouse), and only 'unlocks' the draggable panel for mouse interaction while a modifier key (ALT) is held. When ALT is NOT held, no mouse message is ever forwarded-and-consumed for capture, so the game always retains full mouse control. This lives in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp and is independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003.
steps: In src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp hookedWndProc(): keep the WM_KEYDOWN toggle-hotkey handling as-is. Change the mouse-handling model so that mouse messages are only handed to ImGui for capture when the ALT modifier is held. Detect ALT via GetKeyState(VK_MENU) & 0x8000 (checked at message-handling time). Introduce an atomic bool (e.g., g_altHeld or reuse a clear name) updated so both render() and hookedWndProc agree on the unlock state.

When ALT is held AND the overlay is visible: forward messages to ImGui_ImplWin32_WndProcHandler and consume mouse messages (return 0) so the panel can be dragged - the panel is 'unlocked'. When ALT is NOT held: do NOT consume any mouse message; the overlay is fully passive and the game receives all mouse input normally. Keyboard messages (other than the consumed toggle hotkey) continue to pass through to the game via CallWindowProcW.

Decide and document ImGui input forwarding when ALT is not held: to keep ImGui's internal mouse position roughly current without capturing, you may still forward WM_MOUSEMOVE to ImGui_ImplWin32_WndProcHandler but must NOT return 0 for it (never consume). The critical guarantee is that when ALT is not held, hookedWndProc always falls through to CallWindowProcW for every mouse message so the game never loses the mouse. Pick the simplest approach that guarantees this and comment the reasoning.

In render(): set the ImGui window flags so the panel is only movable while unlocked. When ALT is not held (locked), add ImGuiWindowFlags_NoMove (and consider ImGuiWindowFlags_NoInputs) to the Begin() flags for the 'Bronco - Tradutor##BroncoWindow' window so accidental interaction cannot occur; when ALT is held (unlocked), use the current movable flags (ImGuiWindowFlags_NoCollapse) so the title bar can be dragged. Update the g_wantCaptureMouse / alt-held atomic snapshot in render() consistently with hookedWndProc's reads.

Update the on-screen hint text in render(): the existing welcome message and/or the waiting text should tell the user to hold ALT to move the panel (e.g., 'Segure ALT para mover o painel'). Keep the F8 toggle hint. Use ASCII-only or existing-style strings consistent with the current file.

Ensure hidden/!visible path still clears any capture snapshot (the existing render() early-return already stores g_wantCaptureMouse=false; keep equivalent behavior for the new alt-held state so a hidden overlay never intercepts the mouse).

Update README.md (Uso section) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (overlay module description) to document that the panel is passive by default and only draggable while holding ALT, and that F8 still toggles visibility. ASCII-only, matching existing doc style.
acceptance_criteria: When ALT is not held, hookedWndProc never returns 0 for a mouse message (WM_MOUSEFIRST..WM_MOUSELAST and the NC mouse messages) - every mouse message reaches CallWindowProcW so the game keeps full mouse control.
When ALT is held and the overlay is visible, mouse messages are forwarded to ImGui and consumed so the panel title bar can be dragged.
The F8 (configurable) toggle hotkey continues to be consumed and toggles visibility.
The ImGui window uses NoMove (locked) when ALT is not held and is movable when ALT is held.
When the overlay is hidden, no mouse message is consumed (game is in full game mode).
On-screen hint tells the user to hold ALT to move the panel; README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md document the ALT-to-move behavior.
verification: Static review: trace every code path in hookedWndProc for a mouse message when ALT is not held and confirm it always ends at 'return CallWindowProcW(...)' and never at 'return 0'.

Static review: confirm the alt-held detection (GetKeyState(VK_MENU) & 0x8000) is used consistently and that the atomic used to communicate state between render() and hookedWndProc is read/written without races (store in render, load in WndProc, as with the existing g_wantCaptureMouse pattern).
Static review: confirm render() applies NoMove when locked and movable flags when unlocked, and that the hidden path still prevents capture.
Cannot compile on Linux; do not run cmake. Confirm no C++ syntax errors and that VK_MENU/GetKeyState are available (Windows.h already included transitively via imgui_impl_win32 / config).
findings: Replaced the cursor-over-panel mouse-capture model with an ALT-gated model in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp. Renamed the atomic g_wantCaptureMouse -> g_captureMouse (now stores 'unlocked' state) and added a helper isAltHeld() that returns (GetKeyState(VK_MENU) & 0x8000) != 0. hookedWndProc now computes 'unlocked = visible && g_captureMouse.load() && isAltHeld()'; only when unlocked does it forward mouse messages to ImGui and consume them (return 0). When locked-but-visible it forwards ONLY WM_MOUSEMOVE to ImGui without consuming (never returns 0). Traced every mouse path when ALT is not held: all fall through to CallWindowProcW, none return 0, so the game always keeps full mouse control. WM_KEYDOWN toggle hotkey handling unchanged (still consumed). render() now applies ImGuiWindowFlags_NoMove|NoInputs when ALT is not held (locked) and ImGuiWindowFlags_NoCollapse (movable) when ALT is held; it stores altHeld into g_captureMouse each frame. The hidden early-return still stores g_captureMouse=false, and toggleVisibility() clears it on hide. Added a persistent on-screen hint 'Segure ALT para mover o painel. F8 liga/desliga.'. Documented the ALT-to-move / passive-by-default behavior in README.md (Uso) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (overlay module). Verification was static review only: this is a Linux sandbox with no MSVC/Windows SDK/DirectX/vcpkg, so the DLL cannot be compiled or run (per context.json). GetKeyState/VK_MENU are Windows APIs available transitively via imgui_impl_win32/config includes. No lingering references to g_wantCaptureMouse remain.
